description:
Network Audio/Video in OBS-Studio using NDI technology

DistroAV is an OBS plugin that add support for NDI technology for network audio/video. The DistroAV plugin support features to receive NDI (NDI Source), transmit the OBS Preview/Output to NDI (NDI Output) and transmit an OBS Source or scene to NDI.
In short
- This release support the new OBS 33+ plugin location (Windows installer & Portable)
- MacOS : IMPORTANT : Switch your installation to the DistroAV tap for homebrew - Important, as distroav cask on homebrew (default repo) will be disabled soon
- This has a few fixes but a lot of underlying required work for the dev-team
What's Changed
- Add A/V sync logging behind compile time switch by @BitRate27 in #1462
- Fix NDI frame resize mid stream from Teams by @BitRate27 in #1464
- General small fixes by @Trouffman in #1466 & #1459
- Remove forbidden filename chars from NDI names by @BitRate27 in #1468
- Simplify check for supported pixel format (no temp NDI sender) by @BitRate27 in #1470
- CI: Explicitly set the permissions for GH actions by @Trouffman in #1473
- Move to new obs_properties_add_button2 by @BitRate27 in #1481
- Add developer documentation by @BitRate27 in #1496
- Add web_control_url property to ndi source (obs-ptz integration) by @BitRate27 in #1460
- Handle unsupported-CPU NDI init failures as “not loaded” in plugin state/UI by @Trouffman with @Copilot in #1486
- Add full control of output using obs-websockets by @BitRate27 in #1472
- Update Brew tap link to new name by @Trouffman in #1500
- macos build improvements - clean package ID & less hardcoded values by @Trouffman in #1503
- CI: Set time-limit + bump runner version by @Trouffman in #1504 & #1506
- Add new plugin location (OBS 33+) for windows installer and portable by @Trouffman in #1508
- AGENTS.md: Relax instruction to never commit by @glikely in #1509
- Set timestamps before sending frames to NDI (receiver performance) by @BitRate27 in #1505
- Update plugin to 6.2.2 by @Trouffman in #1512
New Contributors
- @glikely made their first contribution in #1509
